idea: Custom AI agent build for research teams
buyer: Heads of research at funds and consultancies
pain: Off-the-shelf tools do not fit their workflow
v1: One working agent for one team's workflow
verdict: Good fees and warm demand, but she is not a production engineer and support obligations follow the build.

why.distribution: Direct to heads of research she knows, who have live AI budgets.
why.demand: Firms are commissioning exactly this right now, though the market is filling with agencies.
why.fmf: She understands the workflow deeply but is not a production software engineer; builds need contracted help.
why.revenue_structure: Project builds; maintenance is a follow-on she would have to sell separately.
why.defensibility: Dev shops and consultancies compete directly, and the platforms keep absorbing the middle.
why.leverage: Each build is bespoke; patterns transfer but code rarely does cleanly.
why.time_to_revenue: Scoping and a first build: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: The strongest budgeted trend available to her.
why.ceiling: £22k x 9 builds = £198k gross, less 40% to contracted developers.

ceiling_arithmetic: £22k x 9 builds = £198k gross, less ~40% to contracted engineers = £120k net. The direct-cost deduction is what keeps this off the target even at full tilt.
carries: Live budgets, a warm buyer, and a genuine understanding of the workflow being automated.
kills: She subcontracts the actual product, so the margin leaves and the delivery risk stays.
test: Ask three heads of research what they tried to build internally and failed at.
test_pass: One offers to pay for a scoped build.
test_fail: They have an internal engineer or an agency already.
